title: Hasan of Basra and the Feather Robe

full_text:
Hasan was a gentle, honest coppersmith of Basra who lived in modest comfort with his aged mother. A wicked Persian alchemist named Bahram, seeking the hidden treasures of the Mountain of Clouds, tricked Hasan onto his ship and carried him across stormy seas to a colossal sheer mountain of black magnetic stone.

The alchemist sewed Hasan inside a camel hide; a giant Rukh bird seized the hide, carried it to the mountain summit, where Hasan retrieved the alchemical herbs, but the cruel alchemist abandoned him upon the peaks!

Hasan cast himself into the mountain stream, survived the precipice, and found refuge in the magnificent Palace of the Seven Maiden Princesses, who adopted him as their beloved brother.

While the maidens were absent, Hasan beheld Princess Manar al-Sana, daughter of the Supreme King of the Jinns, who flew to the palace lake with her sisters in feather robes. Hasan fell deeply in love, married her with her consent, and brought her home to Basra to live in happiness with his mother.

However, during Hasan’s absence on a trade journey, the feather robe was discovered, and the princess flew back to the forbidden Islands of Waq.

Hasan set forth on an epic, impossible quest across seven continents, passing through the Mountain of Fire, crossing the Sea of Thorns, and winning the aid of giant kings through his unshakeable piety.

He reached the Islands of Waq, solved the king’s three impossible riddles of wisdom, liberated his beloved wife, and returned to Basra amidst grand celebrations, proving that pure devotion and faith overcome the most formidable enchantments.
moral: A pure heart, filial piety, and relentless devotion conquer the darkest sorceries and liberate the captive.

options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
